full_judgment:
Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 186 of 2004 directed the Special Judge to treat Julfikar Ali and his wife Rahima Ali as accused in the case and to take cognizance against them under the relevant provision of law' and thereafter to proceed with ti1eCase in accordance with law. 

 21. The learned Special Judge took cognizance against Julfikar Ali and Rahima Ali pursuant to the judgment and order passed by the Appellate Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 186 of 2014. Under article 111 of the constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh the direction given by the Appellate Division to the court below is binding upon it and the subordinate courts are duty bound to comply with the same. If the Court does it may not only the contemptuous but also tantamount to violation of the constitution. The learned Special Judge pursuant to the order of the Appellate Division took cognizance and framed charge against Julfikar Ali and Rahima Ali and in such a situation it is not necessary to accord sanction from the Commission for prosecution of accused Julfikar Ali and Rahima Ali as per provision of Rule 15 (3) of Rules 2007. 

 22. Rule 15 (3) of the Rules 2007 is not applicable in this particular case in view of the direction and observation given by the Appellate Division in Criminal Petition for leave to Appeal No. 186 of 2014. Moreover neither the Commission nor the Special Judge have any scope to ignore, avoid and not to comply the decisions or observations made, by the Appellate Division. If they do so, definitely it will be clear violation of the constitution and they be also liable to face the contempt proceeding Article 112 of the Constitution Provides that all executives and judicial authorities shall act in aid of the Supreme Court. Those authorities must comply and, act in accordance with the orders and directions given by either Division of the Supreme Court. [Reference: Amzad Hossain vs State, 62 DLR (AD), 288]. 

 28. However, it has come to our notice from the materials annexed to the application, which Mr. Mahbubuddin has also drawn out attention, that the learned Special Judge after receiving the order of the Appellate Division passed in Criminal Petition for leave to Appeal 186 of 2014 by an order dated 11-6-2015 corrected the charge sheet inserting the names of Md Julfikar Ali and Rahima Ali in the column of the accused deleting their names from the column of the witnesses. We cannot approve such act of the learned Special Judge. He has no authority to correct the charge sheet. Pursuant to the order of the Appellate Division, he ought to have straight way took cognizance against the said persons without making any correction of the charge sheet and then proceed further. However, by such improper act of the learned Judge the accused persons will not be prejudiced in any manner and, as such they have nothing to be aggrieved.
